goal_objective: Advance fix/quota-ledger-indexes: Remove the global provider-call ceiling: every provider request on the platform reserves and settles through one exclusive quota-ledger transaction, and on the append-only production ledger (128k baselines, 278k reservations) each admission full-scans both tables, holding the lock ~240 ms. Index the hot admission queries so the lock hold is a few milliseconds and the cost no longer grows with ledger age.. Acceptance criteria: AC1: A fresh SQLite ledger has indexes on baselines (account_scope, quota_group, dimension, window_seconds, observed_at), reservations (account_scope, quota_group, dimension, created_at), reservations (account_scope, quota_group, dimension, window_started_at) and reservations (account_scope, state, lease_expires_at).; AC2: An existing SQLite ledger created without those indexes gains them on first use, keeps every row, and the coordinator still reserves and settles on it.; AC3: SQLite's query plan for each hot admission query (baseline lookup, rolling settled-usage sum, rolling and fixed pending counts, identity-keyed reservation lookup, expired-lease sweep) searches an index instead of scanning the table.; AC4: A PostgreSQL ledger without the indexes gains them on first use, and re-running the upgrade is a no-op.; AC5: Exact-source feature CI and the staging exhaustive gate are green before promotion; production deployment waits for the human's approval.. Required local profile: docker_integration. Stop at ready_for_human_review; do not integrate, promote, deploy, or modify another worktree.
